catalog_quote: [p.7] All syllables begin with a consonant (including the glottal stop) and are open. ... [p.8] Lengthened vowels are interpreted (and represented) as a sequence of two (geminate) vowels, but not two syllables, because they are stressed when they occur word final the same as any other VV series. ... Stress normally occurs on the penultimate syllable. However, if the ultimate syllable is CVV, stress occurs on the first V as shown in (19). (19) tapʰéda 'morning' čokʰára 'many' mikʰía 'rancid' waibía 'big'. Certain meaning differences are encoded only by contrastive stress. (20) če-hí 'come (PST)' čé-hi 'come (IMP)' mí-a 'I (ERG)' mi-á 'I (DAT)'. ... [p.3] In the practical orthography and in texts, stress is written only where it is grammatically imposed, overriding the general stress rules. ... audit.recode_to: No change to kind (weight-hedged, right edge, CVV heavy). Update srule from 'not described' to: secondary stress on the word-initial syllable in words of four or more syllables (Harms 1984 §4.2 p.186); optionally cite Harms 1984 §4.1.1 p.183 for the final-CVV rule being exceptionless ('sin tener en cuenta las consideraciones gramaticales').
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation (Harms 1994 pp.7-8, exx. 18-20; p.3; pp.19-20) is verbatim in the held PDF, verified against scanned and the p.8 page image. (2) Deciding source is the 1994 SIL reference grammar by the language's principal fieldworker, the top item in Glottolog's descriptive list; StressTyp2 and WALS rest on the same author. The only better-targeted work is Harms's own 1984 phonology (Sistemas fonológicos 5), which I fetched sources from the SIL archive via Wayback, scanned (spa, 200 dpi, sequential) and read: it confirms primary stress (penult by default, final if the last syllable is CVV, grammatical conditioning by word class, contrastive pairs) and adds a secondary-stress rule (initial syllable, words of 4+ syllables) that our record lists as undescribed. sources.quote: p.173: 'el acento en epena pedee siempre cae en la última o penúltima sílaba de la palabra ... la segunda vocal en una secuencia nunca lleva acento.' p.183 §4.1: 'el acento es contrastante a nivel de palabra' (wára 'hijo' vs wará 'sabroso'); 'en una sílaba del patrón CVV, la primera vocal de la serie lleva el acento mayor.' §4.1.1: 'Todas las palabras que terminan con el patrón CVV llevan acento en esa sílaba sin tener en cuenta las consideraciones gramaticales' (tobíã, ʔopʰóo, waibía). §4.1.2: verbs penult in imperative, final in other moods; adjectives final (with non-phonemic final lengthen
sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of Epena Pedee (45 pp, same fieldworker); states the final-CVV rule as exceptionless and describes secondary stress (initial syllable of 4+-syllable words), which our record marks 'not described'. fetched sources now.
